name: Eneabba Rare Earths Refinery
location_description: Eneabba, Western Australia (brownfields site at Iluka's existing Eneabba operation)
description: Australia's first fully integrated rare-earths refinery (Eneabba Phase 3): roasting, leaching, purification, solvent extraction and product finishing, producing separated Nd, Pr, Dy and Tb oxides - 'one of the few rare earths refineries operating outside of China' on commissioning. Capacity (AR25 p.57): 16.0 ktpa REO output on Eneabba stockpile feed (max 18 ktpa contained REO feed); 23 ktpa total REO capacity with all circuits on blended feed; FID (2022) modelled 17.5 ktpa. Owned and operated via Iluka wholly-owned SPE Iluka Eneabba Pty Ltd ('RefineryCo'). FID 3 Apr 2022 at A$1,000-1,200M and 2025 start; AR25: capital estimate now A$1.7-1.8B with >A$1B spent or committed (A$1,134M to date, A$443M in 2025), engineering >95% complete, civil works substantially complete, all major equipment ordered (roaster kiln due H1 2026), SMPEI contracts to be awarded H1 2026; commissioning 2027. Feedstock: Eneabba stockpile initially; Wimmera as potential future feed; third-party concentrates under contract from Northern Minerals (Browns Range) and Lindian (Kangankunde, 10% of capacity for 15 years). Offtake: binding customer agreements still being negotiated (A$400M EFA tranche conditional on offtake). Metallisation feasibility study to conclude in 2026; magnet-waste recycling at the refinery assessed as technically viable (2025 desktop study).

name: USA Rare Earth Wheat Ridge Separation Facility
description: Separation capability that has demonstrated production of commercial-grade Dy and NdPr oxide from recycled feed. Future Serra Verde concentrates are described as part of the planned oxide-production feedstock base; commercial scale not established from public disclosures.

name: Less Common Metals
description: Rare-earth metal and alloy producer through which USA Rare Earth operates its metallization capability.

name: USA Rare Earth Stillwater Magnet Facility
description: First commercial sintered NdFeB magnet-production line commissioned in March 2026. Aerospace and defense are among the stated target markets.
